newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Boeing-MD merger won't impact Taiwan buying plans.
newsitem.headline: Boeing-MD merger won't impact Taiwan buying plans.

text.p: Taiwan's major airlines said on Monday that Boeing's absorption of McDonnell Douglas would bolster U.S. aerospace competitiveness, but not influence their own aircraft purchasing plans.
"Boeing and McDonnell each has its strong point and their merger should strengthen their capability to attack Airbus," Steve Yang, spokesman for Taiwan's largest carrier China Airlines, told Reuters.
Europe's Airbus Industrie is Boeing's chief rival in the commercial aviation arena.
EVA Airways, a unit of shipping giant Evergreen Marine and Taiwan's second international carrier, called the deal positive for post-merger Boeing.
"No doubt about that, the merger can strengthen their competitiveness," said EVA spokesman Nieh Kuo-wei. "They can save costs in research and development and many other ways."
Both Taiwan airlines said the merger would not cause them to switch to Airbus from Boeing or McDonnell Douglas, or influence their purchasing plans.
"We will not change our plan to buy mid- and short-haul planes from Airbus," Yang of China Airlines said.
China Airlines has 14 Airbuses in its 43-plane fleet and hopes to build its fleet total to 67 planes by 2003. Of the total, 12 to 15 will be Airbuses, Yang said.
Yang said China Airlines was considering buying planes from Airbus or Boeing.
"We are now evaluating whether we should buy the Airbus 330, Airbus 340 or Boeing 777 for our long-haul, mid-capacity planes," Yang said without giving further details.

Earlier on Monday EVA acknowledged for the first time an imminent plane purchase from both Boeing and McDonnell Douglas, but declined to confirm local media reports that it would buy six planes worth US$1 billion or more.
"We do have plans to buy planes from both Boeing and McDonnell Douglas, but I cannot give details now," EVA spokesman Nieh Kuo-wei told Reuters by telephone.
"So far their merger has not influenced our current plan to buy planes from them. I believe Boeing and McDonnell will make their operations clear after the merger," Nieh said.
EVA said in May it was considering buying 10 or more Boeing 747-500 passenger planes, worth some US$200 million each.

EVA now owns 28 planes -- 12 Boeing 747-400s for long-haul international routes, five Boeing 767-300s, four Boeing 767-200s, six McDonnell Douglas MD-11s and one newly delivered MD-90. EVA took delivery in October of the first of six MD-90 planes bought from McDonnell Douglas in 1995.
Boeing and McDonnell Douglas said in Washington on Sunday they would merge to create the world's largest aerospace company, in a deal worth about $13.3 billion.
